South should look towards hearts for the 2 extra tricks he needs. Playing to the ♥Q is almost certain to produce only 1 extra trick. If South plays a heart to dummy's ♥10, however, he will take 2 heart tricks whenever the ♥J is held by West. If South crosses in clubs to play the ♥10 from North, if East has the ♥J, he will cover, holding South to 1 heart trick.

1-B14.explanation: West leads the ♠K against 4♥. After the defense cashes 3 spade tricks and plays a club, South must ruff and take the rest of the tricks. This should be easy if diamonds break no worse than 4-2. The 4-1 trump break means that care must be taken. If South draws East's remaining trumps, he will also be out of trump himself. The blockage in diamonds will result in defeat when diamonds are 4-2. before drawing any more trump. The lead is in the South hand and the remaining diamonds can be cashed.

1-B15.explanation: West leads the ♥10 against 6NT. After the defense takes the ♥A and continues hearts, South must play the club suit for no losers. He must play the suit by leading the ♣Q. If West plays low, dummy plays low, and East's ♣J is pinned. South still has a finessing position over the ♣K. If West covers the ♣Q with the ♣K, the ♣A is won as East follows with the ♣J. South now has a finessing position over West's ♣9.

1-B16.explanation: West leads the ♥10 against 6NT. After the defense takes the ♥A and continues the suit, South must play the club suit for no losers. Second, he can cash the ♣A playing either defender to have a singleton ♣K. Cashing the ♣A works on two distributions of the defenders' clubs, while leading the ♣Q works on only one distribution. Therefore, cashing the ♣A is the correct play.

1-B17.explanation: West leads the ♥10 against 6NT. South should win the opening heart lead and play on clubs. South can afford to lose 1 trick in clubs, but not 2. The only problem can occur when one defender has all 3 outstanding clubs. If West follows with the ♣5, a low club is played from dummy. If West discards on South's club lead, the ♣A is played from North. A club is led towards South's ♣Q, holding East to 1 club trick. and play a club towards his ♣Q. If East plays any club, South has an easy time. If East discards, South can play either a low club or the ♣Q and later finesse against West's other club honour.

1-B18.explanation: West leads the ♥10 against 6NT. South is faced with playing the club suit for 1 loser. As the ♣A must always be lost, South cannot afford to lose a trick to the ♣Q. and West follows with the ♣6, South must decide whether to play dummy's ♣K or a low club. Playing the ♣K from dummy will work for only one distribution of the defenders' clubs, when East has a singleton ♣Q. is a superior play because it works in two cases.  This play will succeed when East has the singleton ♣A and when West has all 3 clubs. In the latter case, East will discard. South can cross back to his hand and again lead clubs through West.

1-B19.explanation: West leads the ♠K against 4♥. After the defense takes 3 spade tricks and switches to clubs, South must play the trump suit for no losers. South should plan to finesse East for the ♥K. and plays a heart, covering East's card. West's discard marks the 4-0 trump break. South plays another diamond to dummy and finesses hearts again. South must return once more to dummy to play hearts through East a third time. South can accomplish this by ruffing his ♦A. draw the last trump, and take the rest of the tricks.

1-B2.explanation: West leads the ♥K against 4♠. After the defense takes the first 3 heart tricks and switches to clubs, South must win the ♣A and take the rest of the tricks. South will have to find a way to dispose of his 2 club losers. If East holds the ♦A, South can make the contract with the help of a play known as a ^*Bruffing finesse^*N. and leads a diamond. If East covers with the ♦A South can ruff and later use dummy's 2 remaining diamonds for club discards. There are plenty of trump entries to reach the diamond winners in dummy. South discards a club. When West cannot win this trick, another diamond is played from dummy for a second ruffing finesse. As long as East has the ♦A, he is powerless to defeat the contract. If West was dealt the ♦A, South can never make the contract.

1-B20.explanation: West leads the ♠J against 4♥. South must lose tricks to the ♥A, ♥K, and ♣A. He must play to avoid a loser in spades. If, after winning the spade opening lead, South plays hearts immediately, he will be defeated. The defense will win and continue spades. South will be unable to avoid the loss of a spade trick. After winning the opening spade lead, South unblocks the ♦A and ♦Q and leads a club. Dummy's ♣K and ♣Q make for a certain entry. The defense will win the ♣A and continue spades. cross to dummy in clubs, and discard his ♠5 on the ♦K. South then concedes 2 trump tricks to the ♥A and ♥K.

1-B21.explanation: West leads the ♠Q against 4♥. South should not play dummy's ♠K. Against a suit contract, West would not lead the ♠Q if he also held the ♠A. On the given lie of the cards, South's play in spades does not matter. The defense will take 3 spade tricks and then play a club to South's ♣A. If South is fortunate, he can establish and enjoy North's diamonds to discard his losing clubs. South should win 2 heart tricks in the closed hand, making sure to preserve dummy's ♥Q. When hearts prove to be 3-2, half of the battle is over. cashes the ♦K, and trumps a diamond in his hand. When diamonds are 3-3, South can draw the last trump with dummy's ♥Q and play the good diamonds to discard his club losers.

1-B22.explanation: West leads the ♥K against 4♠. It looks as though only 3 losers exist, the ♠A, a heart trick, and a diamond trick. If South ruffs the second heart lead and tries to knock out the ♠A, East will duck the first 2 spade tricks. East will take his ♠A and play another heart, forcing South's last trump. East will now have a second trump trick and the contract will fail. South can guard against a 4-1 trump break by discarding a diamond at trick 2. South has a diamond loser anyway and by losing it early, he is able to retain trump control. Assume the defense switches to clubs and South wins. South plays trump, East holding up as before. South now has one more trump than East. South can trump the heart return and draw East's last trump. South has all winners remaining.

1-B23.explanation: West leads the ♥K against 7♠. Souths wins the ♥A and appears to have no losers. He should try to draw trump immediately so that the defenders do not get any ruffs. and ♠K and must get back to the closed hand to draw the last trump. There is some danger in trying to return to the South hand with the ♣A. As East and West have only 3 clubs between them, it is not unlikely that one of them will be void. If the player with a club void has a trump left, the grand slam will be defeated. After cashing a top diamond, South can afford to ruff the second diamond with the ♠Q or ♠J as long as trumps are 3-2. South uses his remaining trump honour to draw the last trump and takes the balance of the tricks.

1-B24.explanation: West leads the ♥A against 4♠. The defense takes the first 3 heart tricks. South ruffs the next heart lead and has only to dispose of his club loser. After cashing the ♣A, South should be careful to ruff his ♣2 with the ♠A. If the ♣2 is ruffed with the ♠Q, the spade suit is blocked. After cashing the ♠A, North will have only diamonds left. South will go down if diamonds are 4-1 as the defense will be able to ruff the second round. South gives himself an easy way back to his hand to draw trump. South can overtake the ♠Q with the ♠K, draw trump, and take the balance.

1-B26.explanation: West leads the ♠K against 4♥ South starts with 9 top tricks (the ♠A, 7 heart tricks, and the ♦A). The ♦Q may be worth a trick, via a finesse, if West has the ♦K. The contract will be in danger only if East has the ♦K and the defenders can take 2 spade tricks. If South wins the ♠A in dummy, East will later be able to lead a spade through South's ♠J if he can win the ♦K. The ♠J will be trapped and the contract will fail. South can draw trump and take the diamond finesse. but the ♠A stops that suit. North's long diamond can take care of South's second spade loser.

1-B29.explanation: West leads the ♠K against 2♥. West cashes the 2 top spades East plays a trump, won in dummy. South still has certain losers in both diamonds and clubs. South should try to ruff his second club loser in the dummy. and surrenders a club trick, the defense will play another heart. The other 3 tricks can be taken in clubs if the ♣Q can be picked up. South can cash the ♣A and ♣K hoping clubs are 2-2 as above. However, your contract would still be safe if East had won the trick. East is not the dangerous opponent and now your ♦J has been promoted into the extra winner that you need. If West wins the ♦Q, he can take two more Spade tricks and your contract is defeated.

1-M104.explanation: West leads the ♦K against your contract of Two Spades. and have a Heart loser, two Diamond losers and two Club losers. Win the ♦A, play a Spade to dummy's ♠A and a small Spade back toward your hand. If East plays the ♠Q all is well. 1-M112.explanation: West leads the ♥Q against your contract of One No Trump. one in Diamonds, and two in Clubs. The two extra tricks will have to come from the Club suit. If South now cashes a top spade in dummy and crosses to the ♠A, East's ability to follow to both rounds will reveal a complete count of the hand (West must be 5431). If West has the ♥9 the contract can no longer be made. West will discard his remaining spade and dummy will be ^*Bone suit squeezed^*N in hearts. If the ♥8 is discarded South will be able to take only one heart finesse as the suit will be blocked. West will be able to cover the ♥10 with the ♥K and take a trick with the ♥9. Refusing to cash the ♣Q is no better. As before, West can cover the ♥10 with the ♥K and take a trick at the end with the ♥9. The entry gained can be used, for example, to counter the threat of a one suit squeeze. The ♣Q will now squeeze West instead of North. If West throws a heart, the spade loser that was just created is thrown from dummy. 4 heart tricks can now be taken by leading the ♥10 on the first round. the ♥8 is discarded from dummy. South can take one heart finesse immediately. The South hand now contains another spade entry to take a second heart finesse.

5-A24.bidding_sequence: (东)pass-(南)pass-(西)1♦-(北)pass-(东)1♠-(南)2♣-(西)pass-(北)2♠-(东)pass-(南)3♣-(西)pass-(北)pass-(东)pass-
5-A24.explanation: West leads the ♦A against 3♣. After West cashes 3 rounds of diamonds and continues the suit, South should attempt to count the hand before playing from the dummy. West would have opened the bidding 1♥ if he had 5 hearts. Since East must have 5 hearts, he must, therefore, also have 5 spades. If East had less than 5 spades, he would have responded 1♥ not 1♠. East's shape is probably 5521 (6520 is also possible). as East will probably be able to ruff low. West will still have a trump trick. South should, therefore, ruff with the ♣10 and plan to squeeze East in the majors. East will have to have the ♥K, a card he has probably shown in the bidding and with his signal at trick 3. To retain a hand entry in clubs, which is necessary for the squeeze to function, South must duck either the first or the second round of clubs to West. Depending on which round of clubs is ducked and what suit West returns, a ^*Bsimple squeeze^*N or a ^*Btrump squeeze^*N will develop against East. South can draw the last trump and cash another club pitching a heart from the dummy. East is trump squeezed. East must either bare his ♥K (South cashes the ♥A, ruffs the third spade, and scores the ♥Q) or come down to 3 spades (South ruffs out the spades and returns to the ♥A to cash the long spade). South must win the ♥A. A trump squeeze is no longer possible. However, West's heart return has effectively performed a ^*BVienna coup^*N. East will be simple squeezed on the run of the clubs.

5-A25.explanation: West leads the ♠10 against 4♥. West's spade lead goes to East's ♠A. goes to South's ♠J and is ruffed by West. West gets out with a trump. West's Unusual Notrump overcall and the early play have marked him with 1255 distribution. As East is known to have only 2 diamonds, his trump will make it impossible to ruff 3 diamonds in the dummy. When South leads the ♥Q, drawing East's last trump, West is squeezed. If West pitches a diamond, South's ♥Q holds. South can now establish a diamond trick by ruffing. North overtakes with the ♥K and a club trick can be set up by ruffing in the closed hand. There are several possible play sequences. South might as well concede a diamond right away. West wins the ♦A and returns a club (he needs to have both the ♣K and ♣Q for the squeeze to function). and a club is ruffed by South. After cashing the ♠K, a diamond is ruffed low in the dummy. Dummy's last spade is ruffed by South. South has achieved a suitable matrix for the entry shifting squeeze. The ♥Q is played leaving West with no answer.

5-A26.bidding_sequence: (南)1♥-(西)2NT-(北)4♣-(东)pass-(南)4♠-(西)pass-(北)5♦-(东)pass-(南)6♥-(西)pass-(北)pass-(东)pass-
5-A26.explanation: West leads the ♠J against 6♥. South can easily succeed if West has 2-1 or 1-2 in the majors simply by winning the opening lead, drawing trump, and playing on spades. This line of play will not work if West is 1-1 in the majors. East will have to gain the lead at some point in spades. East will return a diamond through South's ♦Q (West is very likely to have the ♦K) and North's ♦A will be knocked out. South will no longer have the timing to ruff both his club losers in the dummy while drawing trump and setting up and cashing a long spade. West cannot profitably attack the ♦A entry. South should duck the opening lead. If West switches to a low diamond South should duck this around to his ♦Q. South wins the ♣A and ruffs a club. Next, he draws 2 rounds of trumps with the ♥K and ♥Q. Now, South takes the spade finesse and cashes the ♠A. After ruffing his last club in the dummy, South ruffs a spade. South can draw East's last trump and use the ♦A as an entry to the winning spade in the dummy.

5-A27.bidding_sequence: (北)1♣-(东)pass-(南)1♥-(西)pass-(北)2♥-(东)pass-(南)4NT-(西)pass-(北)5♦-(东)pass-(南)6♥-(西)pass-(北)pass-(东)pass-
5-A27.explanation: West leads the ♦Q against 6♥. East wins trick 1 with the ♦A and returns a diamond won by the ♦K. South draws trump, noting that West began with 2 hearts. South should run his trumps. On the second last trump West will be forced to abandon either spades or clubs. If South can read the position, a double squeeze will be established. a spade is also thrown from dummy. The ♠K and ♠A are cashed next. The last trump will squeeze both defenders, West in diamonds and clubs and East in spades and clubs. a spade is thrown from dummy as before. The ♣K and ♣A are cashed next. On the last heart both defenders will be squeezed, West in diamonds and spades and East in clubs and spades.

5-A28.bidding_sequence: (北)1NT-(东)pass-(南)3♠-(西)pass-(北)4♣-(东)pass-(南)5♠-(西)pass-(北)7♠-(东)pass-(南)pass-(西)pass-
5-A28.explanation: West leads the ♥J against 7♠. West's heart opening lead is won in the dummy. The only possible problem is a 5-1 club break. South should assume that West has 5 clubs and play for a ^*Bcompound squeeze^*N. If East has 5 clubs there is no hope. A fourth round of trump is played. If West started with 5 clubs, he will be forced to abandon either hearts or diamonds on this trick. as East rates to be longer than West in both hearts and diamonds. The position in hearts and diamonds is identical. Assume for the sake of argument that West abandons diamonds. South pitches from dummy in the suit he judges West has unguarded. and continues with a club to the dummy. East showing out is the only relevant case. South cashes the winner in the suit West has abandoned. The last club winner is cashed for a discard in the suit guarded by both defenders. On the last trump, West is squeezed in clubs and hearts while East feels the pinch in diamonds and hearts.

5-A29.bidding_sequence: (北)1♦-(东)pass-(南)3♣-(西)3♦-(北)pass-(东)4♣-(南)4NT-(西)pass-(北)5♠-(东)pass-(南)7NT-(西)pass-(北)pass-(东)pass-
5-A29.explanation: West leads the ♣10 against 7NT. West's club lead is won by South as East discards a diamond. South might as well cash a top diamond at trick 2. It seems that each defender bid their void in an attempted major suit takeout. West is presumably 5503 leaving East with 4450 distribution. On the run of the clubs the defense will be subject to a ^*Bcompound squeeze^*N. and East must abandon either spades or hearts (a diamond discard is immediately fatal). The position in spades and hearts is identical. Assume for the sake of argument that East discards a spade. South can arrange for a double squeeze with hearts being the suit guarded by both defenders. The ♠A is cashed followed by the ♦A and a diamond to the South hand. West in spades and hearts and East in diamonds and hearts.

5-A3.bidding_sequence: (南)1♥-(西)2NT-(北)3♣-(东)pass-(南)3♠-(西)pass-(北)4♣-(东)pass-(南)4NT-(西)pass-(北)5♥-(东)pass-(南)6♥-(西)pass-(北)pass-(东)pass-
5-A3.explanation: West leads the ♠4 against 6♥. After winning the opening lead and drawing trump, South appears to have a loser in both diamonds and clubs. West has shown at least 5-5 in the minors with his Unusual Notrump bid. West is very likely to have both the ♦A and the ♣K. East thus guards the third round of diamonds and a simple squeeze against West will not work. South can make the contract on a strip squeeze. South begins by leading the ♦2. West must duck and North wins the ♦Q. South runs all of his spade and heart winners, counting West's discards. West must pitch a diamond. South can now exit the ♦K. West must lead away from his ♣K.

5-A30.explanation: West leads the ♠J against 6NT. West's opening spade lead is overtaken by East. South has only 11 top tricks. East should be allowed to win at trick 1 in an attempt to rectify the count for a squeeze. East shifts to a heart won in dummy. When East discards, his most likely shape is 7330 (West rates to be longer than East in both hearts and diamonds). If that is the case, the defense will be subject to a ^*Bcompound squeeze^*N. overtaking the last round with North's ♣A. East must keep his spades and must, therefore, give up his guard in either hearts or diamonds. West will have the only heart guard. A double squeeze will operate with diamonds being the suit guarded by both East and West. South crosses in diamonds and cashes the ♠A. A heart is played to the dummy and the last club will squeeze both defenders, East in spades and diamonds and West in hearts and diamonds. Again there will be a double squeeze, but this time hearts will be the suit guarded by both defenders. South crosses in diamonds. West will be squeezed in diamonds and hearts on the play of the ♠A. East will be squeezed in spades and hearts when the other top diamond is cashed.

5-A31.explanation: West leads the ♥Q against 3NT. West's heart opening lead is taken by East with the ♥A. East returns a heart. South has 8 top tricks, 4 in spades, 1 in hearts, and 3 in diamonds. at first glance it appears South needs a favorable diamond lie or a successful guess in clubs to make the contract. West continues hearts, East follows and South wins the ♥K. South should next cash 4 rounds of spades, followed by the ♦A. South then exits with his remaining heart. South should be careful to keep exactly 1 club in dummy. If West is able to exit in diamonds, dummy wins. The contract will only be in danger if West began with exactly 4441 distribution. South must exit with dummy's club before cashing the last diamond winner. West will win the ♣A and be endplayed into giving dummy the last 2 diamond tricks. This plan will also work if West's singleton club is the ♣Q. It will fail, however, if West's club is a smaller card. (or the ♣Q) by cashing dummy's last diamond winner before leading dummy's club. If East follows small, South must put up the ♣K. South cannot afford to lose the lead to West (who has the ♦J to cash).

5-A32.bidding_sequence: (西)1♦-(北)pass-(东)pass-(南)加倍-(西)pass-(北)2♦-(东)pass-(南)2♥-(西)pass-(北)4♥-(东)pass-(南)pass-(西)pass-
5-A32.explanation:
West leads the ♣Q against 4♥. East wins trick 1 with the ♣A and switches to the ♠10. West covers with the ♠J and dummy wins the ♠K. South's 2 spade losers are not going away so South must avoid the loss of a trump trick. South's chances are much better if he can engineer a 3 card ending where the defense is on lead and must give up their natural trump trick. West must have the ♦Q and South should finesse in that suit immediately, first cashing the ♦K. After cashing dummy's ♦A for a spade pitch, dummy's last diamond is ruffed. and ruffs his last club in dummy. South 
exits a spade, endplaying West. West can do no better than to cash his other spade trick and lead the ♥Q, a card he is known to hold. and finesse East for the ♥J. If West held that card he would have a balanced 15 point hand and probably would have opened the bidding with 1NT.

5-A33.explanation: West leads the ♠10 against 6♠. West's trump lead is won by South. South should cash the top hearts immediately and ruff a heart in dummy. The 3-3 break is good news but South is not out of the woods yet. ruff a diamond to the closed hand and play trumps from the top. The contract will make whenever trumps are 3-3. If this is the case, South still has a chance by exiting with the fourth round of trump. If East has the ♣K and began with 1 or 2 diamonds he will be endplayed. South should not cash dummy's ♦A. He should lead a small diamond instead and ruff in his hand. To prevent East from unblocking his spades and avoid being endplayed, South should be careful to ruff with the ♠4. Despite East's efforts to unblock, South's ♠2 is just low enough to lose the lead to East. With East holding the ♣K, he is endplayed into giving South a way to dispose of his 2 club losers.

5-A34.bidding_sequence: (南)2♣-(西)pass-(北)2NT-(东)pass-(南)4NT-(西)pass-(北)5♥-(东)pass-(南)7♦-(西)pass-(北)pass-(东)pass-
5-A34.explanation: West leads the ♠K against 7♦. West's spade opening lead is won in dummy. South's only possible loser is in clubs. If hearts are 3-3, there will be no problem. If hearts do not break the squeeze chances are excellent since West is certain to hold the ♠Q. South should cash the top hearts. If East has heart length, the contract is guaranteed on a ^*Bdouble squeeze^*N. On the last diamond West must abandon clubs to keep his ♠Q. Dummy discards the ♠J and East is squeezed in hearts and clubs. If West has the ♣Q or ♣J, however, a ^*Bguard squeeze^*N will develop. On the last diamond West is forced to bare his ♣J. Dummy discards from either major. and finessing against East's ♣Q. There is no ambiguity in the ending as West's last 2 cards are both known. If West had started with both the ♣Q and ♣J, the position would have been equally clear. An opponent is squeezed in 3 suits. In 1 of the threat suits, the victim is protecting his partner against a finesse. There are no entries in either of the other threat suits, preventing a simple squeeze from maturing.

5-A35.bidding_sequence: (南)1♠-(西)pass-(北)3♠-(东)4♥-(南)4NT-(西)pass-(北)5♦-(东)pass-(南)6♠-(西)pass-(北)pass-(东)pass-
5-A35.explanation: West leads the ♥7 against 6♠. West's heart lead is taken by East. East continues hearts. South can afford to ruff high. When West follows it appears that South should have discarded a club at trick 2. Dummy has more than enough trumps to take care of South's 3 small clubs. South can, therefore, afford to draw 1 round of trump on which East discards. and a club ruff in dummy. South should cross back to his hand by leading a heart and ruffing high. West's discard confirms the heart count. South leads another low club. South will either be able to establish the clubs or to cash the ♣K and cross ruff. When West ruffs in front of dummy, South must overruff with the ♠Q. West's remaining trump will prevent South from ruffing his last club loser. South is forced to draw trump and play for a squeeze. On the last spade, East is subject to a guard squeeze. He must keep a heart winner and 2 clubs. East must therefore discard his diamond honor. South cashes his remaining high club (discarding dummy's heart) and finesses diamonds through West. In one of the threat suits, the victim is protecting his partner against a finesse. There are no entries in either of the other threat suits, preventing a simple squeeze from maturing. For a guard squeeze to work against the defender to the right of the squeeze card, the threat in the hand with the squeeze card must contain a winner.

5-A36.bidding_sequence: (西)pass-(北)1♦-(东)pass-(南)2♣-(西)pass-(北)3♣-(东)pass-(南)3♥-(西)pass-(北)4♦-(东)pass-(南)6♣-(西)pass-(北)pass-(东)pass-
5-A36.explanation: West leads the ♠K against 6♣. West's wins trick 1 South's only loser is in hearts. He will need either a 3-3 diamond break or some kind of squeeze to succeed. and probe the diamond distribution by cashing 2 of dummy's top diamonds. When West turns out to have diamonds stopped, a squeeze becomes necessary. If West has both heart honors he will be the victim of a simple squeeze between hearts and diamonds. South should run his trumps, taking care to discard the ♥J and to keep dummy's remaining spade. West has no good answer. A diamond discard is immediately fatal. A discard of the ♥K will create a finessing position against East's ♥Q. East becomes the only defender with a spade stop. South discards dummy's small diamond. When South cashes dummy's last diamond winner, East is squeezed in the majors. 1 of these suits is stopped by both defenders, but by discarding from that suit, the victim exposes his partner to a simple squeeze. In a second threat suit, the squeeze victim is protecting a finessing position against his partner. In the third threat suit the victim is the only defender with a stopper.

5-A4.explanation: West leads the ♣J against 4♥. West's club lead is taken by East. East returns a club, won by South. South needs 3-2 trumps and East to have the ♦K. South must play carefully to handle a 4-2 diamond break. South should duck a diamond at trick 3. South wins the trump return, draws a second round of trump, and crosses in spades. South now takes the diamond finesse, cashes the ♦A, and if a diamond is still outstanding ruffs his last diamond in dummy. South will lose a trump trick at the end.

5-A5.bidding_sequence: (东)1NT-(南)2♥-(西)加倍-(北)2♠-(东)加倍-(南)3♦-(西)pass-(北)pass-(东)加倍-(南)pass-(西)pass-(北)pass-
5-A5.explanation: West leads the ♦8 against 3♦ doubled. West has announced length and strength in hearts. East sounds like he has the spades locked up. South's only real chance is to play East for a hand like the above and try to set up dummy's spades. A spade is played to the ♠K and ♠A. Ducking the first round of spades to West would allow West to shift to a club, defeating the contract. won in the dummy so that South can take a spade ruff. After cashing the ♥A and ruffing a heart, another spade is ruffed by South. A spade trick is conceded to East. East is left with the only remaining trump, but no matter how he defends, he will only take the ♣A in addition to his master trump.

5-A6.explanation: West leads the ♠7 against 4♥. West's spade lead is won by East. The defense continues spades and South must ruff the third round. and East holds off. The second round of trumps is also allowed to hold. The 4-1 trump break threatens South's trump control. South must stop playing hearts. South's only chance is that East has 4423 distribution. South unblocks his top diamonds and plays 3 rounds of clubs. The ♦A is now played. South overruffs and plays a club. East will get just his ♥A. If East discards so does South. Again East will get only the ♥A.

5-A7.explanation: West leads the ♠3 against 6♣. It looks like a ^*BMorton's Fork coup^*N. South will eventually lead the ♥4 placing West on the horns of a dilemma. South can discard the ♥Q on dummy's spade winner and concede just a diamond trick (diamonds must be 3-2 for the contract to have a chance). If West takes the ♥A, South will have a discard in hearts as well as spades. South will not lose a diamond trick. East might duck. South would be forced to discard too early, destroying the Morton's Fork. and ruffs in the closed hand. South draws 1 round of trumps, making sure to play the ♣5 from dummy, and plays the ♥4. West has to make his decision before South. If West ducks, South wins the ♥K and sets up a spade trick for a heart discard. South will lose only a diamond trick. North has a discard available in hearts for 1 of South's diamonds. North has sufficient trump entries left to set up and also enjoy a spade winner for another diamond discard.

5-A8.bidding_sequence: (北)1♣-(东)pass-(南)1♠-(西)pass-(北)2♣-(东)pass-(南)2♦-(西)pass-(北)3♦-(东)pass-(南)3NT-(西)pass-(北)pass-(东)pass-
5-A8.explanation: West leads the ♥J against 3NT. West's opening heart lead is won by South. South does not have time to establish the diamonds as the defense will be able to cash their hearts first. South must play on clubs, but if a trick has to be lost in that suit, dummy's lack of a quick side entry could spell trouble. South should cash his top spades pitching diamonds from the dummy (cashing only 1 high spade also works). The top clubs are cashed next. If the ♣Q is still outstanding, South concedes a club trick as he discards his other heart honour. If the defense plays either spades or diamonds, the South hand will become high and only 3 more tricks will be lost.

5-A9.explanation: West leads the ♠K against 5♥. After East overtakes West's ♠K and returns the suit, South has a decision to make. East has shown 8 spades and West is likely to have the ♥Q. In that case, if South ruffs low, West will be able to overruff. The contract will probably fail if diamonds are 4-1. and finesse West for the ♥Q. East's discard means that there is still a trump loser. South should now cash 2 top diamonds. When East discards again the contract seems to be in trouble. South continues with 3 rounds of clubs, ruffing the third round. South's trumps have been shortened to the same number as West's. Next he cashes dummy's third diamond winner and leads North's remaining spade discarding South's diamond loser. West must also discard. East has only black cards left and will smother his partner's ♥Q whatever he returns.

5-B1.bidding_sequence: (南)2♣-(西)2NT-(北)pass-(东)3♦-(南)3♥-(西)pass-(北)4♥-(东)pass-(南)6♥-(西)pass-(北)pass-(东)pass-
5-B1.explanation: West leads the ♥9 against 6♥. West's trump lead is won by South. West's unusual no trump has shown at least 5 cards in both diamonds and clubs. As East bid diamonds, he must have longer diamonds than clubs, making a club ruff prone to an overruff. The ♦2 is played, forcing West to duck. North wins the ♦Q. South draws trump, pitching a diamond from dummy on the last round. South now cashes 3 rounds of spades, ending in the dummy. A spade is played and ruffed by South. West must keep the ♦A and 3 clubs. West must lead a club away from the ♣Q. Even if West plays the ♣Q, blocking the suit, dummy will be high. This ending would not have worked if South had not gone to the trouble of setting up a spade winner in the dummy.

5-B10.explanation: West leads the ♥6 against 4♠. East wins the first 2 heart tricks and gives West a heart ruff. West exits a diamond, won in dummy. South must hope to pick up the trump suit If East has 3 or more diamonds, he will guard that suit and the squeeze will not function. If East has 3 or more clubs, South lacks the dummy entries to isolate the club threat and have an entry at the time of the squeeze. South plays all but 1 of the trumps. a diamond discard from West gives up an immediate trick. A club discard will allow South to set up a club trick by ruffing. Dummy has a diamond entry to reach the winning club.

5-B11.explanation: West leads the ♠K against 6♥. West wins the opening spade lead and continues the suit, South ruffing. West's bidding has shown a very strong 2 suiter in spades and diamonds. West certainly has the ♦K. West's discard marks the 4-0 trump break. South must time the play carefully. Four rounds of clubs are cashed, throwing a diamond from dummy on the fourth round. South crosses in hearts and plays a spade from dummy. If South had tried a spade from dummy before cashing the clubs, East would have discarded a club, leaving South no chance. South overruffs and cashes the rest of North's hearts. On the last trump West is squeezed.

5-B12.bidding_sequence: (西)2♠-(北)加倍-(东)pass-(南)4♦-(西)pass-(北)4♠-(东)pass-(南)5♣-(西)pass-(北)5♦-(东)pass-(南)5♥-(西)pass-(北)7♣-(东)pass-(南)pass-(西)pass-
5-B12.explanation: West leads the ♠K against 7♣. West's lead of the ♠K  goes to the ♠A. West is marked with the ♠Q. South's only chance is to play East for the ♠10. In that case, South will be able to execute a ^*Bdouble trump squeeze^*N. The ♥2  is discarded from the South hand on the fourth round of clubs. The diamond suit is cashed next. On the last diamond, a spade pitch from West will allow South to ruff out the ♠Q and return to the ♥A to cash the ♠J. West must part with a heart and East is similarily squeezed. East must pitch a spade. South now plays the ♠J, covered and ruffed. the ♠9 is high and the ♥A can be used to reach it.

5-B13.bidding_sequence: (南)1♠-(西)pass-(北)2♦-(东)pass-(南)3♠-(西)pass-(北)4♠-(东)pass-(南)6♠-(西)pass-(北)pass-(东)pass-
5-B13.explanation: West leads the ♥Q against 6♠. West's heart lead is won by South. A top trump is cashed. When West discards, South will have to arrange for a trump endplay against East. and a heart is ruffed. South crosses again in diamonds, noting the fall of West's ♦J. Dummy's last heart is ruffed. South's spade length is reduced to that of East. West discards confirming the diamond count. East must now be 4342 for the contract to have a chance. South cashes a top club and crosses to dummy in clubs. Dummy's fourth diamond is cashed as South discards his last club. East will ruff low and South underruffs. East must lead away from the ♠Q at trick 12. If West had followed to the third diamond, South would have to cash 3 rounds of clubs, ending in the dummy. The thirteenth diamond will endplay East in trumps as before.

5-B14.bidding_sequence: (东)5♦-(南)5♠-(西)pass-(北)6♠-(东)pass-(南)pass-(西)加倍-(北)pass-(东)pass-(南)pass-
5-B14.explanation: West leads the ♠Q against 6♠. West's trump lead is won by South. South should cash another high trump which reveals the 3-1 break. West must have the ♣A to go with his trump trick for his double. West has at most 1 diamond given East's 5 level preempt. To accomplish this, dummy will need 4 heart entries along with the ♦A. and a club is ruffed. South plays a heart and when West follows low, the ♥10 or ♥9 is played from dummy. If East discards, South will have no trouble scoring all 4 of his small trumps by ruffing clubs as West follows. another club is ruffed. South crosses to the ♦A, cashes the ♥Q, and plays a third club, ruffing in hand. South exits a trump to West. West is down to all clubs. He will exit with the ♣A, ruffed by South. North has an entry in hearts to reach the ♣K.

5-B15.explanation: West leads the ♦K against 4♠. West's lead of the ♦K  marks him with the ♦Q and East with all the remaining high cards for his 1NT opening. South must win as a heart shift from West would immediately sink the contract. South can go a long way towards solving both of these problems by leading a club from dummy. When East covers, South discards a diamond. South must now find a way to get to the dummy. South can guard against this possibility by leading the ♠8 or ♠9 and, when West discards, overtake with the ♠10 in dummy. and return the ♠4. South allows dummy to win and plays clubs for heart discards. On dummy's third club winner, East will ruff with the ♠7. South can overruff and cross in trumps to enjoy the rest of the clubs.

5-B16.explanation: West leads the ♥Q against 4♠. West's opening heart lead goes to the ♥A. South can guarantee the contract by playing for an elimination. South begins by drawing 2 rounds of trump in the closed hand. The ♥2 is ruffed, eliminating that suit. and exits with a low club. East must win and shift to a diamond to cause any trouble. Trumps are drawn, ending in the South hand and the ♦A is cashed for a heart discard. The ♦J is played, covered by West as the last heart is pitched from North.
